summary: Reviewed all 7 modified files: gui/public/css/styles.css, src/orchestration/workspace-orchestrator.ts, src/orchestration/repository-orchestrator.ts, src/orchestration/workspace-health.ts, and all three test files.

CSS changes (AC 1–4): The two alias tokens --badge-credential-set and --badge-credential-set-bg are correctly placed in the :root block immediately after --badge-clean-bg, with a well-written comment explaining the semantic alias relationship and the reason for independence. .credential-badge--set correctly uses var(--badge-credential-set) and var(--badge-credential-set-bg). Visual equivalence is guaranteed — the aliases resolve to the same computed values as their underlying tokens in both light and dark themes. Dark-mode handling is correctly omitted (var() cascade handles it).

Credential success logging (AC 5–7): Both orchestrators implement an identical pattern — after a successful git clone and only when credential !== null, a Source:'credentials', Severity:'info' log entry is appended with accurate Context (ProjectId, WorkspaceId, RepositoryId) and a human-readable message. The guard correctly skips the entry for SSH clones where credential is null. Pattern placement (after clone success check, before return) is architecturally sound.

Stale badge suppression (AC 8–10): checkWorkspaceHealth() queries the error log by source:'credentials', filters to the correct workspace+project scope, then uses a Set-based de-duplication loop over newest-first entries to inspect only the most recent entry per repository. Issues a credential-missing health issue only when the most recent entry has Severity:'error'. A newer Severity:'info' entry cleanly suppresses the stale badge without deleting history.

@remarks JSDoc (AC 10): The checkWorkspaceHealth() @remarks block precisely describes the stale badge resolution mechanism including the newest-first ordering and Set de-duplication logic. New @remarks blocks on createWorkspace() and addRepositoryToProject() document the credential success logging behaviour.

Tests (AC 11): All three test files have thorough, well-isolated coverage. The stale badge suppression tests correctly use two-entry arrays (error + info in one order, then reversed) to validate both suppression and re-surfacing. SSH no-log tests use fake git binaries with null-credential path. Test naming is clear and descriptive.
No blocking issues found. One Fix-Forward improvement applied (see reviewer-applied-fix comment). One Documentation-Forward item tagged.

comments.note: No blocking or architectural concerns found. All four Review Dimensions — Maintainability, Best Practices, Performance, Future Context — are satisfied. The credential success logging and stale badge suppression are cleanly modelled as an event-log state machine (newest-first, Set de-dup), which is a correct and idiomatic pattern for this codebase.

The Set-based de-duplication approach in checkWorkspaceHealth() is a particularly clean design choice: it leverages the existing 'newest-first' ordering guarantee from errorLogManager.list() to avoid any sorting overhead, and is O(n) in entries. Future extension to additional severity levels (e.g. 'warning') would require only a trivial conditional change. Well done.

The Developer's note about extracting a shared logCredentialSuccess() helper if a third orchestrator gains the same pattern is well-reasoned. The current duplication is minimal (two call sites, identical shape), and the trade-off between premature abstraction and DRY is correctly resolved by leaving it in place. No action required.

[documentation-forward] The @remarks block on createWorkspace() documents credential success logging but does not mention that the written log entry is queryable via checkWorkspaceHealth() to suppress the stale credential-missing badge. Cross-referencing the health check function in the @remarks would help future readers understand the full lifecycle. Similarly for addRepositoryToProject().
